newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel says bank talks on track.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says bank talks on track.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc said on Monday there were no problems with its bank lenders on a financial restructuring and expected to agree the details in time for shareholders to vote by the end of June.

"There are no problems with the banks," a Eurotunnel spokeswoman said. Eurotunnel earlier said its bank syndicate had agreed to extend a payment standstill on 70 billion francs ($12.4 billion) of junior debt to December 14, 1997.
Co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle said on January 20 he hoped to agree restructuring terms by March, in time to send documents to its 225-strong bank syndicate.

"Working parties are studying the details of the various financial instruments and fixing the parameters," the spokeswoman said. That included agreeing the conditions for implementing the instruments, she said.
The standstill extension was not to allow for further bank negotiatons but was due to a fire which seriously damaged part of the Tunnel in November and disrupted operations.

The terms of the restructuring, which had been agreed in principle last October with steering committee banks, need to be concluded by the end of March so that a prospectus could be sent out in the first two weeks of April, to allow shareholders to vote on the complex package by June 30, the spokeswoman said.

Eurotunnel also wants to include in the package a formal reply from the French and British governments to its request for an extension on its 65-year concession. A longer operating licence would change the profile of the restructuring.
The company wants to have freight traffic on its Le Shuttle service reinstated, as well as a return to full commercial service, before seeking shareholders' approval for the restructuring.
The company invoked the debt standstill in September 1995 and the freeze would have ended on March 14 without the extension.

The restructuring includes a swap of eight billion francs of bank debt for Eurotunnel shares, leaving stockholders with 54.5 percent of the equity capital. But banks can also exercise conversion rights on equity notes which would take out a further eight billion francs of debt and dilute shareholders down to 39.4 percent.
